adoption.notes: Ships the profile set and a dormant registry that cites this contract; packaged skill Tier D triggers remain the live Tier D path until the cutover.

hunks.summary: The ratification gate: a candidate becomes ratified only when its dossier is complete under ratification.md, where v1 required that its open questions be closed, plus the qualification-fixture exception that lets a pair named by an accepted fixture with an open session evaluate and actuate. A changed gate, a new actuation path and a new companion document.
A reset of a pair that no longer holds the authority to evaluate is refused with no_evaluation_authority, before the ordinary refusals, and actuates nothing. A new refusal and its precedence.
The neighbouring-contracts table: the evidence row adds which authority licensed a trip, and rows for ratification.md and safety-qualification-fixture/v1, documents this version froze without.

The battery_emergency_cutoff migration row now names supply-transfer/v1 and migrates the trigger to Tier A until a skills-package/v3 amendment lands, where v1 migrated it to a Tier C proposal. A changed migration.
Legacy action names: a pointer to skills-package/v3, which this version froze without, for the package-facing half of the rule.
Consumer obligations: the qualification exception lifts one activation check for one pair for a bounded window. Part of the exception above.
The error table gains no_evaluation_authority for reset. A new rejection reason.

An Open Questions note: the runtime adapter now requires calibration and reduces a frequency-aligned window to an RMS current, and what stays unproven is accuracy on the target, window geometry, clipping and hardware coverage. It updates a description of the implementation, states no rule, and changes no profile, activation check or verdict. The text it replaced was already false for the consumer frozen here: the calibrated adapter (ori-runtime dac8101b) is an ancestor of 5d14895a, so the correction makes v1 describe what shipped and changes nothing it requires.
The source-transfer open question now points at supply-transfer/v1, which this version froze without, and says a transfer is never a profile outcome.

notes: Every shipped profile is a candidate. Ratification and its dossier are safety-profile/v2's, with ratification.md as its companion document.
